paper.title: Learning with a Budget: Identifying the Best Arm with Resource Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Best Arm Identification with Resource Constraints (BAIwRC), stochastic consumption
unmapped: L types of resources, each pull of arm k consumes random amounts D_{l,k} in [0,1] of each resource; budgets C_l must hold with certainty; the learner knows the budget vector C (no fixed number of pulls)
consumption distributions in class C_{b_l, sigma_l^2}: support in [0,1], |D - E D| <= b_l a.s., Var <= sigma_l^2; reward and consumptions arbitrarily correlated; mean consumptions unknown
settings.definition_quote: An instance of Best Arm Identification with Resource Constraints (BAIwRC) is specified by the triple $Q = ([K], C ,\nu= \{\nu_k\}_{k\in [K]})$. ... We assume that $r_k\in[0, 1], \forall k$, and $R_k$ is a 1-sub-Gaussian random variable. In addition, we assume that the marginal probability distribution of $\{D_{\ell, k}\}_{k\in [K]}$ belongs to the class ... The agent aims to choose a strategy $(\pi, \tau, \psi)$ to maximize $\Pr(\psi=1)$ ... subject to the resource constraint that $\sum^\tau_{t=1} D_\ell(t) \leq C_\ell$ holds for all $\ell\in [L]$ with certainty.

unmapped: L types of resources; each pull of arm k consumes a deterministic unknown amount d_{l,k} in (0,1] of resource l; budgets C_l must hold with certainty; the learner knows the budget vector C
settings.definition_quote: including a special case where $\Pr(D_{\ell, k} = d_{\ell, k})=1$ for all $\ell \in [L], k\in [K]$, which means all the resource consumption amounts are deterministic.

unmapped: L types of resources with arbitrary consumption distributions (means in (0,1]) identical across the instances; budgets C_l must hold with certainty
settings.definition_quote: In instance $Q^{(i)}$, pulling arm $k\in [K]$ generates a random reward $R_k\sim \mathcal{N}(r^{(i)}_k, 1)$ ... Pulling arm $k\in [K]$ consumes a random variable $D$ units of resource $\ell$, following (consumption model)

unmapped: L types of resources; each pull consumes Bern(d_{l,k}) units of resource l with small means d_{l,k}; budgets C_l must hold with certainty
settings.definition_quote: (1) pulling arm $k\in [K]$ generates a random reward $R_k\sim \mathcal{N}(r^{(j)}_k, 1)$ ... (2) pulling arm $k\in [K]$ consumes $D_{\ell}\sim\text{Bern}(d_{\ell, k})$

symbols.gamma_Q: min over resources l of C_l / H_{2,l}(Q), with H_{2,l}(Q) = max_{2<=k<=K} sum_{a=1}^k f(b_l, sigma_l, d_{l,(a)}) / Delta_k^2 and f(b,sigma,d) = 4b/log(4b^2/sigma^2+1) + d (effective consumption)

conditions: consumption of each resource in class C_{b_l,sigma_l^2} (support in [0,1], |D-ED|<=b_l a.s., Var<=sigma_l^2), sigma_l^2 <= b_l^2

source.label: theorem:upper-bound-of-failure
source.quote: Consider a BAIwRC instance $Q$. The SH-RR algorithm has BAI failure probability $\Pr(\psi \neq 1)$ at most $2LK (\log_2 K) \exp\left(-\frac{1}{4\lceil \log_2 K\rceil}\cdot\gamma^{}(Q) \right)$, where $\gamma(Q) = \min_{\ell\in [L]}\{C_\ell / H_{2, \ell}(Q)\}$, and $H_{2, \ell}(Q)$ is defined in (\ref{eq:sto_H}).

results.notes: Failure probability bound; 'horizon' set to known since the budget vector is an input. Budget C is a vector, encoded inside gamma_Q.

symbols.gamma_det: min over resources l of C_l / H^det_{2,l}(Q), with H^det_{2,l}(Q) = max_{2<=k<=K} sum_{a=1}^k d_{l,(a)} / Delta_k^2 (d_{l,(a)} mean consumptions sorted decreasingly)

source.label: theorem:upper-bound-of-failure-det
source.quote: Consider a BAIwRC instance $Q$ in the deterministic consumption setting, i.e $\sigma=0$. The SH-RR algorithm has BAI failure probability $\Pr(\psi \neq 1)$ at most $K (\log_2 K) \exp\left(-\frac{1}{4}\min_{\ell \in[L]} \{ \frac{C_{\ell}}{\lceil\log_2 K\rceil H_{2, \ell}^{\text{det}}}\}\right)$ where $\gamma^{\text{det}}(Q) = \min_{\ell\in [L]}\{C_\ell / H_{2, \ell}^{\text{det}}(Q)\}$

results.notes: Removes factor 2L relative to Theorem 1 in the deterministic case.

conditions: any strategy satisfying the resource constraints with certainty
Gaussian rewards N(r_k,1) with 1/2 = r_1 >= r_2 >= ... >= r_K > 0; instance Q^(i) flips arm i's mean to 1 - r_i
arbitrary consumption distributions with means d_{l,(k)} in (0,1], identical across instances, arranged as in the construction
holds for some instance i in [K] among the K constructed instances

source.label: theorem:lower-bound-fixed-consumption-multiple-resource
source.quote: When $C_1, \ldots, C_L$ are sufficiently large, such that $96\cdot\text{min}_{i\in [K],\ell\in [L]} \left\{\frac{2 C_\ell}{H^\text{det}_{2, \ell}(Q^{(i)})}\right\} \geq 1$, for any strategy there exists an instance $Q^{(i)}$ (where $i\in [K]$) such that $\Pr_{i}(\psi\ne i)\ge \frac{1}{6}\exp\left(-108\cdot \gamma^{\text{det}}(Q^{(i)})\right)$

results.notes: Minimax-type lower bound over a constructed family of K instances; holds for any consumption distribution.

symbols.gamma_sto_tilde: min_l C_l / tilde H^sto_{2,l}, tilde H^sto_{2,l} = max_{2<=k<=K} sum_{j=1}^k g(d_{l,(j)}) / Delta_k^2
symbols.g: any increasing function with g(0)=0 and lim_{d->0+} 1/(g(d) log(1/d)) = +infinity

conditions: any strategy satisfying the resource constraints with certainty
Gaussian rewards N(r_k,1) with 1/2 = r_1 > r_2 >= ... >= r_K = 1/4; instance Q^(j) flips arm j's mean
Bernoulli consumption Bern(d_{l,k}) with d_{l,(j)} = c*d0_{l,(j)}, c in (0, c_bar) for an identified threshold c_bar
maximum over the two instances j in {1, i} for a fixed i in {2,...,K}

source.label: theorem:lower-bound-sto-consumption-multiple-resource
source.quote: Consider a fixed but arbitrary function $g:[0, +\infty) \rightarrow [0, +\infty)$ that is increasing and $\lim\limits_{d\rightarrow 0^+}\frac{1}{g(d)\log\frac{1}{d}}=+\infty$, $g(0)=0$, ... The following performance lower bound holds for any strategy: $\max_{j\in \{1, i\}}\Pr_{Q^{(j)}}(\psi\neq j) \geq \exp\left(-\tilde{\gamma}^{\text{sto}}(Q^{(j)})\right)$

results.notes: Shows the effective consumption term ~1/log(1/d) cannot be replaced by d for Bernoulli consumption. Statement's dependence on j inside gamma is ambiguous as printed.
